title: Central SLO pipeline for VPC observability: latency, errors, saturation, token throughput
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Problem: Our VPC/private deployment customers currently lack a unified SLO pipeline that combines endpoint latency percentiles, HTTP error rates, node/GPU saturation and end-to-end token throughput into actionable signals. Teams have implemented ad-hoc probes and alerts across clusters; this leads to alert noise, inconsistent autoscaling triggers, and limited correlation between application-level latency spikes and underlying token-saturation events.

Goal: Implement a centralized SLO pipeline and orchestrator for VPC deployments that standardizes health checks, derives composite SLOs, and exposes robust metrics and alerting for: latency (p50/p95/p99), request error rates (4xx/5xx), node/GPU saturation (CPU/GPU/mem), and token throughput (tokens/sec per model instance). The pipeline should integrate with our Terraform IaC modules so customers on Private can opt into the same observability primitives used by Hosted and Dedicated.

Scope:
- Define canonical metrics, labels, and ingestion paths for VPC agents (prometheus exporter conventions).
- Build a centralized SLO service that consumes Prometheus/OTEL metrics and emits composite SLOs and derived indicators (e.g., token_saturation_pct, kv_cache_hit_rate).
- Implement alerting playbooks for: sustained tail-latency (p99 above threshold), rising token-saturation that precedes latency regressions, and error bursts.
- Provide Terraform modules and example configs to install the agent, dashboards, and alerting rules in customer VPCs (non-breaking, opt-in).
- Add deterministic sampling and tags for model variant, sequence-length-bucket, and deployment tier for accurate slicing.

Out-of-scope: per-customer billing integration and runtime kernel selection logic (handled by separate tickets).
acceptance_criteria: Canonical metric names and label schema documented and approved by Observability guild (doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/private-slo-metric-spec).
A deployed SLO pipeline in staging that ingests VPC metrics and produces composite SLO dashboards for latency, error_rate, node_saturation, token_throughput.
Terraform module (modules/observability/vpc) that installs the agent, Prometheus rules, Grafana dashboards, and PagerDuty hooks in a test VPC environment.
Alert rules produce <5% false positives over a 2-week evaluation window while correctly firing on injected fault scenarios (see test plan).

Automated correlation test: when token throughput is artificially driven to >90% of measured capacity, the pipeline surfaces a pre-latency regression indicator within 60s and triggers the autoscaler hook in testbed.
implementation_notes: Metric conventions: use prefix rwinf_ for Redwood Inference internal metrics; token throughput metric name rwinf_tokens_per_sec{model,instance,seq_bucket}.
Latency buckets: store p50/p95/p99 computed by Prometheus histograms + sliding-window decays for faster reaction to regressions.
Saturation signal: derive node_saturation_pct from GPU util, memory pressure, and accept-queue-length with weighted formula (weights to be tuned during staging).
Sampling: add deterministic sampling tag sequence_length_bucket (0-128,129-512,513+). Sampling must be configurable via env var for customer privacy/volume concerns.

Terraform changes: provide backward-compatible module variables; default enable_alerts=false to avoid unexpected PD noise in customer environments. Provide a migration guide for customers who already have custom alerts.

Security: metrics use mTLS and customer-provided KMS for any stored artifacts. No sensitive payloads should be shipped. Confirm with Security on KMS integration if storing aggregated tokens metrics externally.
Observability stack: use existing Prometheus Operator in Private images; where missing, propose a lightweight pushgateway+OTLP collector with rate-limits.
alerts_and_thresholds: latency_p99 > 250ms sustained for 3m => SEV2 alert (action: scale up or investigate tail sources)
error_rate_5xx > 0.2% over 5m => SEV2 (action: circuit-breaker to fallback model variant)
token_saturation_pct > 85% for 90s => warning rule (action: pre-scale and notify infra)
kv_cache_hit_rate drop > 20% relative to baseline for 10m => info alert (action: run cache-eviction diagnostic)
tokens_per_sec_per_instance < 30% of baseline while node_saturation_pct < 50% => potential cold-start or misrouting (investigation alert)
composite_slo_health score < 0.9 over 10m => SEV1 paging with runbook link
test_plan: Synthetic load tests across seq buckets to validate token throughput signals (use loadgen/sim-token-runner PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/loadgen/pull/412).
Fault injection: induce GPU steal and network egress delay to ensure pipeline correlates saturation -> latency in staging.
Alert noise evaluation: run 14-day replay of production metrics (anonymized) and measure false positive rate for each alert rule.
DR test: simulate agent loss in a single AZ and validate failover behavior and aggregated SLO continuity.
